title: EchoChamber
description: A real-time chat application that rewrites messages to match the sender personality type, using an AI model on the backend to adapt tone while keeping the underlying meaning intact.
details: Messages are sent through a lightweight backend that calls an LLM to adjust phrasing based on a selected personality profile before broadcasting them to the room, while keeping the original intent unchanged. The focus of this project was handling real-time updates cleanly on the front end while the rewrite happens asynchronously.

title: NoteFlow
description: A platform where professors can upload course material and students can find and access it in one place, built around simple, role-based access for the two kinds of users.
details: Professors get an upload flow scoped to their own courses, while students get a read-only browsing and search view. Access control is handled at the route level so each role only ever sees the screens meant for it.

title: Mini Compiler
description: A compiler front-end built for my Compiler Design course, covering lexical analysis, parsing and basic semantic checks on a small custom language.
details: The lexer tokenizes source input, a recursive-descent parser builds an AST from the token stream, and a small semantic-checking pass walks that tree to catch type and scope errors before code generation would happen.
